searchText: ~~Is there or will there be a recording of the last AllCoreDev call (#93)?~~ Oh, I can just go watch the "Live Stream" (no longer live) https://www.reddit.com/r/ethereum/comments/i5b0t3/live_ethereum_core_devs_meeting_93_202087_1400_utc/ Do current clients provide a mechanism for JSON-RPC users to easily *notice* when a deep reorg occurs? In the call there is discussion about how exchanges need to protect themselves, but I'm not sure we provide them with the proper tools to do that (e.g., notice a reorg and shutdown). One could write a service that just listens for new blocks from the client and then when it sees a deep reorg fire a notice, but that is pretty round-about. Just saw the hubbub about supply. A couple of people asked me about this on geth discord - now I understand why. Geth can dump out full state of block X iteratively, via json lines, so it's trivial to just pipe it to python to aggregate the total count. <@!211091239112671234> You can dump out a state snapshot at a given block live? Or do you need to stop syncing while it is being dumped? Need to stop it first. Theoretically you can do it via rpc, just the response becomes a bit too large to dump in an rpc response. Plus the db iterator prevents leveldb from modification, so the accumulated writes will blow the system <@!301186049323958275> I have a tool to dump state, it takes a long time. https://github.com/vulcanize/eth-pg-ipfs-state-snapshot Sorry, basically all of the repos are misnamed at this point... as we all know naming this is difficult. we also have this: https://github.com/vulcanize/go-ethereum/blob/statediff_at_anyblock-1.9.11/statediff/doc.go hmmmm: not finished yet etherscan shows 110 million accounts and 112 million eth I assume that etherscan does not delete empty accounts finished <vbuterin> yay!! I run the supply calculation on turbo-geth's slightly out-of-date DB (block 10619322, 1 day 8 hours ago), and I also got 112 million eth (`112094705151351536895834903` wei), but only 96225098 (96.2 million) accounts in the state. And it took 52 minutes (on an SSD disk connected to my laptop via SATA -> USB cable) Maybe we should agree on the same block number to do these tests from? 😛 I think even the block number difference won't explain away 14 million accounts 🙂 Maybe those are the ones that got deleted in the Great State Clearing Of 2016? though I recall the number deleted being 19 million; maybe some got filled back in? I think it is more likely an error in the calculation program somewhere but supply is 112m everywhere This is proving to be an interesting exercise... like a "hello world" of node-based chain analytics ok so <@456226577798135808> tomasz has 9643 more ETH than you, but he is 4606 blocks ahead; from ethereum's recent uncle rate (378 / 6457 yesterday) and average uncle reward (1.65 + 2/32 nephew reward, by sampling https://etherscan.io/chart/uncles), the discrepancy is only 29 ETH Which is within margin of error would be nice to get a full count of block and uncle rewards within that range to see if there is an exact match (hoping there's no self-selfdestructs in that range 😆 ) <tkstanczak> <@456226577798135808> number of accounts in my case is also 96 million - have a look at the screenshot, etherscan must be counting all historically unique addresses even if they have been emptied and touched since creation (re @eth1x_bridge_bot: <Alexey> I think it is more likely an error in the calculation program somewhere)

excerpts.author: holiman
excerpts.content: Just saw the hubbub about supply.  A couple of people asked me about this on geth discord - now I understand why. Geth can dump out full state of block X iteratively, via json lines, so it's trivial to just pipe it to python to aggregate the total count.

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: <@!211091239112671234> You can dump out a state snapshot at a given block live?

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: Or do you need to stop syncing while it is being dumped?

excerpts.author: holiman
excerpts.content: Need to stop it first. Theoretically you can do it via rpc, just the response becomes a bit too large to dump in an rpc response. Plus the db iterator prevents leveldb from modification, so the accumulated writes will blow the system
